daily_reality.summary: Surgical technologists prepare operating rooms, sterilize instruments, maintain the sterile field, pass instruments to surgeons during procedures, and assist with patient positioning and wound closure. They work in hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and specialty clinics.
typical_tasks: Prepare the operating room by setting up surgical instruments, equipment, and supplies
Sterilize instruments using autoclaves and chemical sterilants
Arrange sterile drapes, instruments, and supplies on the back table and Mayo stand
Scrub in and maintain the sterile field throughout the surgical procedure
Pass instruments, sutures, and supplies to surgeons and surgical assistants
Hold retractors and assist with tissue manipulation during surgery
Count sponges, needles, and instruments before and after procedures
Prepare and handle specimens for pathology
Clean and restock the operating room between cases
Transport patients to and from the operating room
Assist with patient positioning on the operating table
key_documents: Sterilization logs and biological indicator results

deadlines.room_setup: Complete before patient arrives in OR (typically 30-60 minutes)
deadlines.surgical_counts: Before incision, before closure, at skin closure
deadlines.sterilization_cycles: Per instrument manufacturer IFU and AAMI standards
deadlines.case_turnover: 15-30 minutes between cases per facility standards

daily_reality.seasonality: Elective surgeries may decrease during holidays and summer vacations. Emergency and trauma surgeries are year-round. End-of-year insurance deductible utilization creates Q4 elective surgery surge.

regulatory.summary: CST (Certified Surgical Technologist) from NBSTSA is the primary national certification. State requirements vary — some require certification, others do not. CAAHEP accredits surgical technology programs. Strict infection control and counting protocols.

key_laws.name: CMS Conditions of Participation — Surgical Services
key_laws.detail: Standards for OR operations, sterile technique, and personnel qualifications

key_laws.name: State Surgical Technologist Certification/Registration Laws
key_laws.detail: Some states require CST certification; others have no requirements
key_laws.status: Varies by state — trend toward requiring certification

key_laws.name: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard
key_laws.detail: OR personnel exposure prevention and sharps safety

key_laws.name: AAMI Standards for Sterilization
key_laws.detail: Standards for instrument processing and sterilization validation

requirements: CST certification from NBSTSA (75 CE credits every 4 years for renewal)
Some states require certification or registration
Clinical rotations covering general, orthopedic, OB/GYN, and other specialties
Trend toward states requiring CST or equivalent for employment
certifying_bodies: NBSTSA — National Board of Surgical Technology and Surgical Assisting
CAAHEP — Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs
NCCT — National Center for Competency Testing (alternative TS-C credential)

regulatory.penalties: Retained surgical items (sponges, instruments) create major liability. Infection control violations lead to facility citations. State board actions for practicing without required credentials.

tools.summary: Surgical technologists work with a vast array of surgical instruments, sterilization equipment, electrosurgical units, and OR management systems. Knowledge of specialty-specific instrumentation is essential.

primary_software.name: Surgical instruments (thousands of types by specialty)
primary_software.purpose: Cutting, clamping, retracting, suturing — organized on back table and Mayo stand

primary_software.name: OR scheduling/management systems
primary_software.purpose: Case scheduling, preference cards, supply management

primary_software.name: Instrument tracking systems (Censis, CensiTrac)
primary_software.purpose: Barcode tracking of instrument sets through sterilization cycle

primary_software.name: Surgical robotics (da Vinci systems)
primary_software.purpose: Assist with robotic-assisted surgery setup and instrument management

primary_software.name: Power tools (drills, saws for orthopedics)
primary_software.purpose: Bone cutting and drilling during orthopedic procedures

primary_software.name: C-arm fluoroscopy
primary_software.purpose: Intraoperative imaging for orthopedic and vascular cases

pain_points: Instrument set complexity (some sets have 100+ pieces)
Supply chain issues for specialty instruments and implants
Preference card management across multiple surgeons
Quick room turnover pressure between cases
Learning new instruments for emerging surgical technologies

terminology.summary: Surgical technologists use extensive surgical, anatomical, and sterile processing terminology covering instrumentation, suture types, surgical approaches, and sterile technique.

key_terms.meaning: Sterile gowned and gloved, working within the sterile field
Area around the surgical site maintained free of contamination
Large sterile table for organizing instruments and supplies
Small sterile tray positioned over the patient for frequently used instruments
Electrosurgical unit for cutting and coagulation
Instrument used to hold back tissue for surgical access
Thread used to close wounds (absorbable vs non-absorbable)
Surgical sponges requiring strict counting protocols
Mandatory counting of needles, blades, and sharps before/during/after surgery
Safety pause to verify correct patient, site, and procedure
Tissue removed during surgery sent to pathology
Surgeon-specific list of preferred instruments, sutures, and supplies
Pre-assembled cart of supplies for a specific procedure

career_psychology.summary: Surgical technologists work in high-stakes OR environments where attention to detail is critical. Median salary $62,830 with 5% growth. Physical demands and emotional intensity of surgery. Clear advancement to surgical first assistant.

career_levels.responsibilities: General surgery cases, basic instrument handling, learning specialty procedures
Independent scrubbing, multiple specialties, complex cases
Cardiac, neuro, robotic surgery specialist, mentoring
Active surgical assisting, retraction, suturing, hemostasis

main_fears: Retained surgical items (sponge, needle left in patient)
Break in sterile technique causing surgical site infection
Being blamed for counts that don't reconcile
burnout_causes: Standing for 8-12+ hour shifts in the OR
Keeping up with rapidly changing surgical technology
growth_motivation: Certified Surgical First Assistant (CSFA) for higher pay and expanded role
Bridge to PA or nursing programs
Industry roles in surgical device sales

market.summary: Median salary $62,830 (BLS May 2024). 5% growth projected 2024-2034 with ~8,700 annual openings. About 119,200 employed. Growing demand from aging population and minimally invasive surgery expansion.
market.job_outlook: 5% growth 2024-2034, faster than average. ~8,700 annual openings.

work_arrangements.shift_patterns: Weekday schedules common but on-call for emergencies required
